Free invoice template: Word and PDF in US Letter, with USD and sales tax

A simple one-page invoice for freelancers, contractors and small businesses. Word file you can edit, a PDF so you can see the finished look, and totals already worked out. Sales tax is shown as a separate line that you can set to your own rate or to zero.

What is in the template

  • Logo box, your business name, INVOICE heading and invoice number.
  • Bill to, From and Invoice details blocks with issue date, due date, terms and PO number.
  • Three sample line items with hours, projects and items, unit prices and a tax rate per line.
  • A sales tax line (sample rate of 7.5% on taxable lines, 0% on one line) and a highlighted balance due.
  • ACH bank transfer details and a notes area for your payment terms.
  • Footer with business name, invoice number and page number.

How to fill it in

First decide whether you charge sales tax

The US has no federal invoice law for ordinary business invoices, and sales tax is set by states and local areas. Many services are not taxed at all; many goods are. The 7.5% in the sample is only an example so you can see how the tax line works. Find out your own situation from your state revenue department or your accountant. If you do not charge sales tax, set every line’s tax rate to 0 or delete the tax column and the tax summary row. Nothing here is tax advice.

Step 1: Fill in your details and the client’s

Replace each [bracketed] item. Use the name you operate under, a mailing address and a billing email. Sole proprietors can show their name instead of a company. If your client needs your tax ID for their records, they will usually send you a Form W-9 to fill in separately; you do not normally have to print your tax ID on every invoice, so leave it off unless the client asks. For the client, use the billing contact and address from their purchase order or contract.

Step 2: Invoice number, dates and terms

Number every invoice from a simple sequence (INV-0001, INV-0002). The issue date is the day you send it. Terms such as Net 30 mean the client has 30 days from the invoice date to pay; put what you agreed in the contract. A due date that is a specific calendar date is clearer than “30 days” alone, so the template shows both. Add the client’s PO number if they gave you one, because many accounts payable departments match invoices to POs and reject ones without a number.

Step 3: Write line items a client can approve

Replace the three sample rows with what you actually delivered. Give each line a plain description (“Landing page design, 2 rounds of edits”), then the quantity, the unit and the unit price. Put dates or ticket numbers in the grey detail line so the client can check the work against their records. Use one row per type of work or per milestone rather than one lump sum, because itemised invoices are paid faster and argued about less.

Step 4: Check the totals

Word will not recalculate the totals. After you edit, check each line (quantity × price), add them for the subtotal, apply the tax rate only to the taxable lines, and add the tax to get the total. In the sample, $950.00 + $1,500.00 + $120.00 = $2,570.00 subtotal; 7.5% tax on the $2,450.00 of taxable lines is $183.75; total $2,753.75. If you have already been paid something, subtract it to get the balance due.

Step 5: Payment details and sending

Replace the sample bank block with your bank name, account name, account number and routing number, or a payment link if you use one. Only send account details to clients you trust, and never put full card numbers on an invoice. Edit the note to include any late fee you agreed in your contract (do not add one the client has not agreed). Save as PDF with File > Save As, email it with the invoice number in the subject line and keep the Word file for your records.

Letter size and Word layout

Both files are set to US Letter (8.5 × 11 inches). If your Word is set to A4 it will use the page size stored in the file, so you do not need to change anything.

Frequently asked questions

Is this invoice template really free?

Yes. Download either file without an email address and use it for your own business.

Can I use it for freelance or contractor work?

Yes. Change the units to hours, days or projects, and delete the tax column if you do not charge sales tax.

Does it work in Google Docs?

The .docx opens in Google Docs and in Pages. Check spacing after opening, since fonts can differ.

Does the template calculate totals?

The Word file does not recalculate. The numbers were checked when the file was made, and the page shows how to re-check them. For automatic arithmetic, use a spreadsheet or the free invoice skill described below.

Is there a UK version with VAT?

Yes: the free UK invoice template uses GBP and 20% VAT.
